newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Sept M2 growth below 19pct yr/yr - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Sept M2 growth below 19pct yr/yr - central bank.

text.p: Growth in Slovak M2 money dipped below 19.0 percent year-on-year in September, after 19.5 percent in August, a National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) official said on Thursday.
"September's M2 growth is below 19.0 percent due to a slightly slower rate of loan expansion," Peter Sevcovic, the head of NBS monetary policy, told Reuters.
Sevcovic said that this was the first time in the past 20 months that Slovak M2 had dipped below 19 percent, after hovering at around 20 percent for most of that period.
He said that while final figures for the volume of loans made in September were still unavailable, year-on-year growth was "below" 19.0 percent, after year-on-year growth of 19.8 percent in August.
The NBS's target for year-on-year 1996 loan growth is 7.3 percent.
"We can very cautiously say that our (money supply) measures might have caused the M2 slowdown, though their full effect will, in my personal opinion, only occur next year," Sevcovic said.
In mid-July, the NBS approved a series of measures aimed at curbing lending by local banks.
The NBS full-year target for 1996 M2 is a year-on-year expansion of around 11.6 percent. The central bank's full-year inflation target is 6.0-7.2 percent year-on-year.
Slovak consumer price inflation was 5.2 percent year-on-year in September, after a 5.6 percent increase in August.
